title: A metaclass, when it is the right tool
prompt:
Implement `class FrozenMeta(type)` enforcing that instances only ever set the attributes DECLARED in the class body annotations:

- setting an undeclared attribute raises `AttributeError` at ANY time (init or later)
- declared attributes are freely settable and readable
- `Vec.brand` must equal 'frozen' on every class using the metaclass (the metaclass itself may set class attributes)
- this must apply to subclasses too — that is why it is a metaclass, not __init_subclass__

tests.name: declared attrs work, undeclared rejected
tests.code:
class Vec(metaclass=FrozenMeta):
    x: int
    y: int

v = Vec()
v.x, v.y = 1, 2
assert (v.x, v.y) == (1, 2)
try:
    v.z = 9
except AttributeError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('undeclared attribute must raise AttributeError')
assert Vec.brand == 'frozen'
print('ok')
tests.hint: In Meta.__new__, read ns['__annotations__'] keys and install a __setattr__ closing over that set.

tests.name: inherited by subclasses
tests.hint: Subclass namespaces carry their own __annotations__; merge with the parents' declared names.
